thread:
incident-bot: CRITICAL alert · service=kv-cache · metric=continuous_batching.queue_depth > 1k for 5m. paging #eng-oncall.

maria (oncall): i'm on it, paging the SRE/plat leads. any known deploys ~2h ago?

josh (sre): saw a batch-config rollout at ~01:34 UTC that increased continuous_batching.max_window to 800ms + removed per-tenant soft-cap. big spike in prefix cache entries -> eviction storms. markers: eviction_rate↑, p95 latency↑, queue_depth↑.

raj (platform): confirmed. change was ff:enable_new_batch_scheduler (released 01:33). It widened batching window and increased max_batch_size to 512. suspect amplification for a subset of high-cardinality tenants.

maria (oncall): ok plan: 1) emergency-toggle the flag global=false 2) smoke canary for 5 low-traffic tenants 3) per-tenant overrides for customers we know rely on larger batches. who can flip the flag?

raj (platform): i can flip. prepping a safe rollback command.

raj (platform): CURL to disable globally:
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood/api/v1/flags/enable_new_batch_scheduler/toggle" 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"enabled": false, "scope": "global"}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout started -> featureflag/enable_new_batch_scheduler disable requested by raj. target: all regions.

josh (sre): i'm watching metrics. dashboards: kv-cache.eviction_rate / kv-cache.kv_ops_per_tenant / kv-cache.queue_depth. set alert if eviction_rate > 200% baseline for any tenant.

tia (support): heads-up — i'll draft notices for impacted customers. which tenants are highest risk?

josh (sre): run this quick query to find top offenders:
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, sum(evictions) as evictions, avg(p95_latency) as p95
FROM metrics.kv_cache
WHERE window > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY evictions DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

josh (sre): current top 3 by evictions: acme-corp, beta-inc, lab-analytics. acme-corp is 40% of the extra churn.

maria (oncall): raj, go ahead with the global disable. josh, watch for rollback side-effects (latency might transiently spike). tia, prepare INC-2026-42 and notify acme-corp + beta-inc as P1.

raj (platform): done — flag disabled globally. deploy-bot: featureflag/enable_new_batch_scheduler -> disabled at 2376543245.

deploy-bot: Completed: 8/8 regions acknowledged.

josh (sre): metrics update: queue_depth falling, eviction_rate trending down. p95 improving for most tenants, but acme-corp still high.

maria (oncall): next step: per-tenant overrides. we want to re-enable the old scheduler for acme-corp explicitly (i.e., keep new scheduler off for them) and allow a controlled canary where needed. raj — can you publish per-tenant overrides?

raj (platform): adding overrides now. sample payload:
```json
{ "tenant": "acme-corp", "flags": {"enable_new_batch_scheduler": false, "batch_max_size": 128} }
```
Applying to list: ["acme-corp","beta-inc","lab-analytics"].

deploy-bot: per-tenant overrides applied for 3 tenants.

josh (sre): after overrides, acme-corp eviction rate down 78% in 3m. Good.

maria (oncall): good. let's re-enable the new scheduler only for a small canary set of 5 tenants (low-traffic) to validate the config change with soft-cap reintroduced. who volunteers to watch the canary for 30 min?

kevin (backup): i'll watch the canary dashboards. add me to pager for the next 30m.

raj (platform): enabling for canary set: canary_tenants = ["canary-001","canary-002","canary-003","canary-004","canary-005"]. Command:
```
POST /api/v1/flags/enable_new_batch_scheduler/toggle
{ "enabled": true, "scope": "tenants", "tenants": [..canary list..] }
```

deploy-bot: canary enable started.

josh (sre): immediate checks: eviction_rate, p95, batch_success_rate, queue_depth per tenant. set temporary alert threshold tighter for canary.

maria (oncall): support, please hold outgoing customer comms until we verify canary stability. tia?

tia (support): acknowledged. i'll hold. i'll update acme-corp/beta-inc with mitigation summary and that we're monitoring. drafting now.

sophia (product): flagging product for follow-up: we need gating on batch scheduler with a tunable soft cap per tenant. schedule a follow-up RFC. cc @maria @raj @josh.

josh (sre): canary tenants look stable at +12m. small increase in batch sizes but no eviction spikes. i'll extend monitoring to 60m and then propose rolling to a broader set with per-tenant soft-caps.

maria (oncall): good incident triage: timeline + actions so far: 01:33 deploy changed batching -> 01:50 alerts -> 01:53 global flag disable -> 01:58 per-tenant overrides for top impacted -> 02:05 canary re-enable for 5 tenants. plan: hold broad rollout, create postmortem with remediation tasks: tighter rollout gating, automated per-tenant soft-cap, runbook update.

sophia (product): i'll own the RFC and coordinate with platform.

maria (oncall): assigning postmortem owner: josh. please include customer-impact section and mitigation timeline. schedule incident review tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

josh (sre): will do. I'll also add a temporary dashboard that surfaces any tenant with eviction_rate > 2x baseline and auto-post to #incidents.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. closing the active paging loop — keep monitoring but no further global action unless metrics regress.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-42 created (status: mitigated). Runbook link: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/kv-batching. Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.

tia (support): outbound notification queued to acme-corp + beta-inc + lab-analytics (template: incident/kv-batching-mitigation).

kevin (backup): i'm on watch for next 60m. ping me if anything odd.

maria (oncall): thanks team. follow-ups: josh postmortem, sophia RFC, raj implement per-tenant soft-cap toggle in the feature flags, tia customer comms. :thumbsup:
